"A character dictionary records bare 你 in plural examples such as 你兩個 (‘you two’) and 你眾人 (‘you all’). These cited examples are from historical works; their frequency or productivity in present-day speech is not established here. This is distinct from the ordinary modern plural construction 你们, formed from singular pronoun 你 with 们."
